content:
If you sell on Etsy or Shopify, Printful and Printify are the two print-on-demand platforms you will compare first — and for good reason. Together they power millions of POD stores, both plug into the same sales channels, and both let you start for free. But they are built on opposite models: Printful prints most orders in its own facilities for maximum consistency, while Printify is a marketplace that routes your orders to competing print providers for maximum margin. This head-to-head comparison breaks down pricing, catalog size, print quality, shipping speed, branding, integrations, and support — with verified 2026 numbers — so you can pick the right one for your store in the next ten minutes.

Pricing & Plans: Which Is Cheaper in 2026?

Printify is cheaper on base product costs; Printful is cheaper if you scale past $12K/year in sales, because its Growth plan becomes free. That is the short answer — here are the details.

Both platforms offer a genuinely free tier: no monthly fee, no credit card required, and you only pay the product base cost plus shipping when an order comes in. The paid tiers are where the models diverge:

  • Printify Premium costs $39/month on monthly billing, or $24.99/month billed annually ($299/year) — the monthly price rose from $29 in early 2026. Premium unlocks up to 20% off every product in the catalog. Printify's own math says the discount pays for itself at roughly 15–17 orders per month.
  • Printful Growth costs $24.99/month with a 14-day free trial, and it becomes free for 12 months once your store reaches $12,000/year in sales. Growth unlocks up to 33% off product pricing, 25% off sample orders, and 9% off branding extras like labels and pack-ins.

On individual items, Printify's marketplace model keeps base prices lower — a standard Bella+Canvas 3001 tee typically lands several dollars cheaper through a well-rated Printify provider than through Printful. Printful counters with deeper percentage discounts on its Growth plan and cheaper samples. For a new seller doing under 10 orders a month, both free plans work fine and Printify's lower base prices win on pure margin.

Product Catalog: Depth vs Breadth

Printify's catalog of 1,300+ products is roughly four times larger than Printful's 300+ products — if you want niche items, Printify wins outright.

Printify's 85+ print providers collectively list more than 1,300 products, from standard tees and hoodies to niche items like pet beds, doormats, candles, and jewelry. If your Etsy strategy involves testing unusual niches, Printify almost always has a provider who prints it.

Printful's catalog of 300+ products across 25+ categories is smaller but curated. Everything in it is produced in-house or through tightly controlled partners, and Printful is particularly strong in embroidery, all-over print apparel, and premium cut-and-sew items. For a focused apparel brand, 300 well-executed products are plenty; for a niche-testing general store, Printify's breadth is a real advantage.

Print Quality: Consistency vs Lottery

Printful delivers more consistent print quality because it controls production in-house; Printify quality depends entirely on which provider you choose.

Printful fulfills the vast majority of orders in its own facilities, which means one QA standard, calibrated printers, and predictable color output across every order. Independent reviews consistently rate Printful's DTG and embroidery output among the best in POD, and reported reshipment rates are extremely low. When something does go wrong, there is one company and one support team accountable for fixing it.

Printify is a network, not a printer. Top-rated providers like Monster Digital and SwiftPOD produce excellent results, but the bottom of the provider list is noticeably weaker. Quality, sizing accuracy, and even packaging can vary between providers. The practical implication: with Printify, you must order samples from your chosen provider before scaling a listing, and you should re-check provider ratings periodically.

Shipping Speed & Fulfillment

Printful's production runs a consistent 2–5 business days with typical US delivery in 5–10 business days; Printify ranges from 2–7 business days of production depending on the provider.

Printful operates around a dozen fulfillment centers across the US, Mexico, Canada, the UK, and the EU, and automatically routes orders to the facility closest to your customer. Flat-rate shipping is predictable, and because Printful controls each center, delivery estimates are reliable enough to promise to customers.

Printify's network spans 140+ facilities in more countries — the US, UK, EU, Australia, China, and Canada — which can mean genuinely local production in regions Printful doesn't cover. The trade-off is that you choose the provider at product setup; there is no proximity-optimizing auto-routing. A US customer can end up waiting on a slower provider if you picked by price alone. Express options exist with some providers, but vetting is on you.

Branding & Customization

Printful offers far stronger branding — custom inside and outside labels, pack-ins, branded packaging, and a branded tracking page; Printify's branding options are limited to select providers.

If you are building a recognizable brand rather than a commodity store, this category is decisive. Printful lets you add woven or printed inside labels, outside labels, pack-ins like stickers and thank-you cards, and custom packaging, so the unboxing experience feels like your brand, not a fulfillment house. Printify supports neck labels and inserts only through certain providers, and options vary. For a premium Shopify brand, Printful's branding toolkit is worth the higher base cost.

Integrations & Selling Channels

Both platforms integrate with Shopify, Etsy, WooCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, and eBay — this category is a genuine tie.

Printify additionally supports TikTok Shop natively, which matters if you sell through short-video channels. Printful adds native Amazon integration, which Printify lacks. Both offer open APIs and mature order-sync, so orders placed in your store flow to production automatically with tracking pushed back to the customer. Setup difficulty is similar on both: connect your store, push products, set retail prices, done.

Customer Support

Printful's support is more effective for order problems because one company owns the entire production chain; Printify's 24/7 support often mediates between you and a third-party provider.

Both platforms advertise 24/7 live chat and email support, and both are responsive for account and integration questions. The difference shows up when an order arrives misprinted: Printful can reprint and reship on its own authority, while Printify must coordinate with the provider that produced the item, which adds time and occasionally friction. At low volume this rarely matters; at hundreds of orders a month, Printful's single-throat-to-choke model saves real hours.

Real Cost Example: A Bella+Canvas 3001 Tee, Sold in the US

On the single most popular POD product — the Bella+Canvas 3001 unisex tee sold to a US customer — Printify's total landed cost is typically $2–4 lower per unit than Printful's, before any paid-plan discounts.

Exact prices shift with provider and size, but a representative 2026 comparison looks like this: through a top-rated US Printify provider, the 3001 base cost plus standard US shipping lands around $13–15 total. The same shirt through Printful typically lands around $15–17. Sell that tee on Etsy at $24.99 and the margin difference is roughly $2–4 per order — which is why margin-first sellers gravitate to Printify. Activate Printify Premium and the 20% product discount widens the gap further; activate Printful Growth and its up-to-33% discount narrows it considerably, especially once Growth becomes free at $12K/year in sales.

Two caveats keep this honest. First, shipping on Printify varies by provider — the cheapest base price sometimes ships from farther away, erasing the savings. Second, Printful's higher cost buys lower defect risk: a single refund-and-reship on a misprinted order wipes out the margin advantage of many cheaper orders. Price the whole system, not just the base cost.

Real-World Scenarios: Which Should You Choose?

Etsy beginners should start with Printify; brand-builders and quality-first sellers should choose Printful; high-volume sellers should use both.

  • New Etsy seller, testing niches on a budget: Start with Printify. The free plan plus the 1,300-product catalog lets you test designs across many product types with the best possible margins. Order samples from 2–3 top-rated providers before committing to one for each product.
  • Shopify brand builder, selling premium apparel: Choose Printful. Consistent print quality, embroidery strength, custom labels, and branded packaging justify the higher base cost when your retail price carries a brand premium.
  • Volume seller doing 50+ orders/month: Run a hybrid. Route commodity tees and mugs through Printify Premium (20% off) for margin, and keep your hero products, embroidery, and branded orders on Printful Growth (up to 33% off, free after $12K/year in sales). Many established sellers do exactly this.
  • International audience: Compare provider locations per product. Printify's 140+ facilities cover more countries, but Printful's auto-routing is more predictable in the US and EU.

Also weighing Gelato? See our Printful vs Gelato comparison (2026) — in-house factories vs Gelato's local production network, and Printify vs Gelato for the marketplace-vs-network angle.

Neither feels right? Gelato is the strongest third option, with 35+ local production hubs and aggressive pricing — see our hands-on Gelato review.

How We Compared Them

This comparison is based on our hands-on reviews of both platforms (linked below), each platform's official pricing and catalog pages as of mid-2026, and cross-checks against multiple independent 2026 reviews for fulfillment-time and plan-change data. Pricing figures reflect published 2026 rates: Printify Premium at $39/month or $24.99/month billed annually, and Printful Growth at $24.99/month with the $12K/year free threshold. We update this page when either platform changes plans, catalog size, or fulfillment networks.

Final Verdict

There is no universal winner, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling something. Printify wins on catalog size and base cost — the things that matter most when you are finding your first profitable niche. Printful wins on quality consistency, branding, and operational simplicity — the things that matter most once you have a brand worth protecting. Because both are free to start, the lowest-risk path is to open both accounts, order one sample of your best-selling product from each, and let the physical products make the decision for you.

faqs.q: Is Printify cheaper than Printful?
faqs.a: Yes. Printify's base product prices are typically several dollars lower per item than Printful's because its 85+ print providers compete on price, and Printify Premium ($39/mo or $24.99/mo billed yearly) takes up to 20% off all products. Printful's Growth plan ($24.99/mo) offers deeper discounts — up to 33% — and becomes free after $12K/year in sales, but its starting base prices are higher.

faqs.q: Which has better print quality, Printful or Printify?
faqs.a: Printful has better and more consistent print quality overall, because it produces most orders in its own facilities under one quality-control standard. Printify quality depends on which of its 85+ independent providers prints your order — top-rated providers match Printful, but weaker ones don't, so sampling before scaling is essential.

faqs.q: Is Printful or Printify better for beginners on Etsy?
faqs.a: Printify is generally better for Etsy beginners: the free plan, 1,300+ product catalog, and lower base prices maximize margin while you test niches. Printful makes more sense once you are building a recognizable brand that benefits from custom labels, branded packaging, and guaranteed print consistency.

faqs.q: Which ships faster, Printful or Printify?
faqs.a: Printful is faster and more predictable on average, with 2–5 business day production and typical US delivery in 5–10 business days. Printify production ranges from 2–7 business days depending on the provider you select, though its 140+ facilities can offer faster local delivery in regions like Asia-Pacific where Printful has no center.

faqs.q: Can I use both Printful and Printify at the same time?
faqs.a: Yes, and many experienced sellers do. A common hybrid strategy routes margin-sensitive commodity products (basic tees, mugs) through Printify Premium while keeping premium apparel, embroidery, and branded orders on Printful. Both integrate with the same Shopify or Etsy store, so orders route automatically to whichever platform hosts each product.

faqs.q: Do Printful and Printify integrate with Shopify and Etsy?
faqs.a: Yes — both platforms offer native integrations with Shopify, Etsy, WooCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, and eBay, plus open APIs. Printify additionally integrates with TikTok Shop, while Printful natively supports Amazon. Setup on both takes minutes: connect the store, push products, and orders sync automatically.

faqs.q: Can I switch from Printify to Printful (or vice versa) later?
faqs.a: Yes. Nothing locks you in — your designs and store stay on Shopify or Etsy, and you simply reconnect products through the other platform and republish the listings. Many sellers start on Printify's free plan for margin, then move hero products to Printful once a design proves it can sell, without changing storefronts.

content:
Printify and Gelato are the two print-on-demand platforms most often shortlisted by sellers who have outgrown the obvious default — or who want to avoid Printful's premium pricing from day one. They look similar on paper: both are free to start, both integrate with Shopify and Etsy, and both rely on networks of production partners rather than owning every printer. But their philosophies diverge sharply. Printify gives you a vast marketplace of 85+ competing print providers and lets you choose who makes what; Gelato hides that complexity entirely, automatically routing each order to one of 140+ production hubs in 32 countries. This comparison breaks down verified 2026 pricing, catalog size, quality, shipping, and support — so you can pick the right engine for your store.

Pricing & Plans: Which Costs Less in 2026?

Gelato+ is the cheaper subscription at $19.99/month billed annually versus Printify Premium's $24.99/month annually — but Printify's deeper product discounts (up to 33% vs up to 25%) can claw that back at volume.

Both platforms start free: $0/month, full catalog access, and you pay only product cost plus shipping when orders arrive. The paid tiers differ in 2026:

  • Printify Premium costs $39/month on monthly billing or $24.99/month billed annually ($299/year) — the monthly rate rose from $29 in February 2026. It covers up to 10 stores and unlocks up to 33% off product base prices (around 20% on most popular items). The discount typically pays for the subscription at roughly 15–17 orders per month.
  • Gelato+ costs $23.99/month or $19.99/month billed annually (~$240/year), with a 14-day free trial. It covers unlimited stores and unlocks up to 25% off products (up to 35% in year one on some promotions), premium mockups, stock images, and branded inserts. Gelato retired its Gold tier in 2026; above Gelato+ sits only a custom-priced Platinum plan for enterprise sellers.

On subscription price alone, Gelato wins by about $60/year on annual billing. On per-unit economics it's closer: Printify's marketplace competition keeps base prices low on commodity apparel, while Gelato's advantage shows up in shipping — local production means shorter, cheaper delivery legs, especially outside the US. A classic cotton tee delivered in the US runs roughly $11.50 all-in on Gelato before your margin, which is competitive with well-rated Printify providers.

Product Catalog: Marketplace Breadth vs Curated Depth

Printify's 1,300+ product catalog is roughly five times larger than Gelato's ~250 products — for niche testing, Printify wins decisively.

Printify's 85+ providers collectively offer more than 1,300 products: standard apparel plus niche items like pet beds, doormats, candles, ornaments, and jewelry. If your strategy is testing unusual Etsy niches, Printify almost certainly has a provider who prints it.

Gelato curates roughly 250 products and executes them well. Its catalog is strongest in wall art — posters, framed prints, canvas, acrylic, and metal prints — where it is arguably the best POD platform in the world, plus a solid core of apparel, mugs, tote bags, phone cases, cards, and calendars. If your store sells art prints or a focused apparel line, Gelato's smaller catalog is a non-issue. If you need odd products, it is a hard limit.

Print Quality: Vetted Network vs Open Marketplace

Gelato delivers more consistent print quality because its production partners are centrally vetted and managed; Printify quality depends on the provider you choose yourself.

Gelato doesn't own most of its printers, but it operates the network like it does: partners are onboarded to shared quality standards, orders are monitored centrally, and output is uniform enough that sellers rarely worry about which hub produced an order. Print quality consistently reviews well, and the wall-art output in particular is regarded as gallery-grade.

Printify is an open marketplace. Top-rated providers like Monster Digital and SwiftPOD produce excellent work, but the long tail of providers varies in print quality, sizing accuracy, and packaging. The burden of vetting — ordering samples, checking provider ratings, re-checking after provider changes — sits with you. Sellers who do that homework can match Gelato's quality; sellers who don't get burned.

Shipping Speed & Local Production

Gelato wins shipping outright: automatic routing to 140+ hubs in 32 countries means most orders are produced in the customer's own country, typically delivering in 2–5 business days domestically.

This is Gelato's structural advantage. When a customer in Germany orders from your US-based store, Gelato prints the item in Germany or a neighboring EU hub — no customs, no transatlantic leg, lower shipping cost, and a much smaller carbon footprint. The routing is fully automatic; you never think about it.

Printify's network of 140+ facilities also spans many countries, but routing is not automatic in the same sense — you choose a provider per product at setup time. A US-optimized product can still ship slowly to European customers unless you configure duplicates with EU providers. For US-only stores, both platforms perform comparably (2–7 business day production on Printify depending on provider); for stores with meaningful international traffic, Gelato's auto-routing is a genuine operational superpower.

Branding & Customization

Both platforms offer modest branding options — this is neither platform's strength, and the category is effectively a draw.

Gelato+ includes branded inserts and packaging options on paid plans, which is a nice touch at its price point. Printify supports neck labels and inserts through select providers only. If premium unboxing (custom boxes, pack-ins, branded tracking) is core to your brand, neither matches Printful — see our Printful vs Printify comparison for that angle.

Integrations & Selling Channels

Both integrate natively with Shopify, Etsy, WooCommerce, Wix, and Squarespace — a genuine tie for mainstream sellers.

Printify adds TikTok Shop and eBay; Gelato adds BigCommerce and has a particularly clean Etsy integration. Both provide open APIs, automatic order sync, and tracking push-back. Setup difficulty is similar on both, though Gelato's flow is slightly simpler because there is no provider-selection step — you pick a product, design it, publish.

Customer Support

Gelato's support resolves production issues faster because one company manages its whole partner network; Printify support mediates between you and independent providers.

Both offer 24/7 chat and email support. The difference is accountability: when a Gelato order arrives misprinted, Gelato owns the resolution. When a Printify order fails, support coordinates with the third-party provider, which adds a hop. For account and integration questions both are equally responsive.

Real Cost Example: A T-Shirt Sold in the US vs in the EU

For a US customer, Printify and Gelato land within a dollar of each other (~$11.50–13 all-in); for an EU customer, Gelato's local production saves $3–6 per order in shipping and days of delivery time.

Run the 2026 numbers on a classic cotton tee. Gelato's US base cost is roughly $6.96 plus ~$4.54 US shipping — about $11.50 delivered. A top-rated US Printify provider lands the same shirt around $12–14 delivered, before Premium's discount. With Printify Premium (up to 33% off, ~20% typical) and Gelato+ (up to 25% off) both active, Printify usually edges ahead on US-delivered commodity apparel by a dollar or two per unit.

Flip the destination to Germany and the math inverts. Printify would need an EU-based provider configured for that product to stay competitive; otherwise you pay international shipping from the US and the customer waits 1–3 weeks. Gelato simply prints in the EU at local rates. Stores with more than ~20% international orders almost always net more profit on Gelato, even with its slightly shallower product discount.

Real-World Scenarios: Which Should You Choose?

US-focused niche testers should choose Printify; international sellers and wall-art stores should choose Gelato; many global sellers run both.

  • New Etsy seller, US audience, testing niches: Choose Printify. The 1,300-product catalog and lowest base costs let you test broadly with maximum margin. Sample 2–3 providers per product before scaling.
  • Seller with EU/UK/global traffic: Choose Gelato. Automatic local production in 32 countries eliminates customs delays and slashes international shipping cost — the single biggest lever on international conversion rates.
  • Wall art, posters, and art print stores: Choose Gelato. Its wall-art catalog (canvas, framed, acrylic, metal) is the strongest in POD, produced locally near your buyers.
  • Volume seller on commodity apparel: Choose Printify Premium for the up-to-33% discount, and vet your providers hard.
  • Hybrid global store: Use Printify for US-bound niche products and Gelato for international orders and wall art. Both connect to the same Shopify or Etsy store, and orders route automatically by product.

Want stronger branding and in-house quality control instead? Read our Printful vs Printify comparison — Printful trades higher base costs for premium branding and consistency. Or see how Printful compares directly against Gelato's local production network in our Printful vs Gelato comparison (2026).

How We Compared Them

This comparison draws on our hands-on reviews of both platforms (linked below), each platform's official pricing pages as of mid-2026, and cross-checks against multiple independent 2026 reviews for plan changes (Printify's February 2026 price rise, Gelato's Gold retirement) and delivery-time data. Figures reflect published 2026 rates; we update this page when either platform changes plans, catalog size, or network coverage.

Final Verdict

Printify and Gelato solve different problems. Printify is the margin and variety machine: the biggest catalog in POD, marketplace-driven base prices, and the deepest discounts — at the cost of doing your own provider quality control. Gelato is the logistics machine: a curated catalog, consistent vetted quality, and an auto-routed local production network that makes international selling feel domestic. Neither choice is permanent — both are free to start — so open both accounts, order one sample of your best seller from each, and let the delivered products and the real per-order math decide.

On per-unit cost it depends: Printify's up-to-33% product discount usually beats Gelato's up-to-25% on US-delivered apparel, while Gelato's local production cuts shipping cost and time on international orders, often making it cheaper overall for global stores.

faqs.a: Gelato is typically faster, especially internationally: local production in the customer's country usually delivers in 2–5 business days domestically. faqs.a: Yes, and many global sellers do. A common setup routes US-bound niche products through Printify (bigger catalog, deeper discounts) while sending international orders and wall art through Gelato (local production, faster delivery). Both integrate with the same Shopify or Etsy store, so orders automatically flow to whichever platform hosts each product.

faqs.q: Does Gelato integrate with Etsy and Shopify?
faqs.a: Yes — Gelato integrates natively with Shopify, Etsy, WooCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, and BigCommerce, plus an open API. Printify covers the same core platforms and adds TikTok Shop and eBay. Setup on both takes minutes: connect your store, publish products, and orders sync automatically with tracking pushed back to customers.

faqs.q: Is Gelato+ worth it over the free plan?
faqs.a: Gelato+ is worth it once its up-to-25% product discount saves you more than $19.99/month (annual billing) — typically around 10–15 orders per month depending on your product mix. Below that volume, the free plan is fully functional: full catalog, all integrations, and unlimited stores. Paid plans also add premium mockups and branded inserts.

Gelato owns nothing but the software: an orchestration layer that routes each order automatically to the best-positioned of 140+ vetted production partners in 32 countries. One bets on vertical integration, the other on distributed logistics. This comparison uses verified 2026 pricing and fulfillment data to show which bet pays off for your store.

Gelato is cheaper on both fronts: Gelato+ costs $19.99/month billed annually versus Printful Growth at $24.99/month, and Gelato's base product prices run roughly 15–35% below Printful's on matching items.

Both platforms are free to start — $0/month, full catalog access, pay per order. The paid tiers:

  • Printful Growth costs $24.99/month with a 14-day free trial, and becomes free for 12 months once your store reaches $12,000/year in sales. It unlocks up to 33% off product pricing, 25% off sample orders, and 9% off branding extras (labels, pack-ins).
  • Gelato+ costs $23.99/month or $19.99/month billed annually (~$240/year), also with a 14-day trial. It unlocks up to 25% off products, premium mockups, stock images, and branded inserts, on unlimited stores. Gelato retired its Gold tier in 2026; enterprise sellers move to a custom-priced Platinum plan.

The bigger gap is base cost. Independent 2026 analyses put Printful's product prices 15–35% above Gelato and Printify on comparable SKUs — the premium you pay for in-house production. Printful's Growth discounts (up to 33%) are deeper than Gelato+'s (up to 25%), which narrows the gap at volume, and the $12K/year free-Growth threshold effectively makes Printful's subscription disappear for established stores. But on day one, unit for unit, Gelato is the cheaper platform.

Product Catalog

Printful's 300+ product catalog is modestly larger and stronger in apparel and embroidery; Gelato's ~250 products dominate in wall art and paper goods.

Printful covers 300+ products across 25+ categories: apparel (including premium cut-and-sew and all-over print), embroidery, hats, mugs, home goods, and accessories. Everything is produced in-house or through tightly controlled partners, so catalog breadth comes with uniform execution.

Gelato curates around 250 products and is genuinely best-in-class in wall art — posters, framed prints, canvas, acrylic, and metal prints — plus cards, calendars, and photo books that Printful barely competes in. For a wall-art or stationery store, Gelato's catalog is the better fit despite being smaller; for an apparel-first brand, Printful's depth and embroidery strength win.

Print Quality & Consistency

Printful edges quality consistency because it controls production in-house — published operations stats show a 0.24% reshipment rate — while Gelato's vetted partner network is close behind and equally reliable for most sellers.

This is the closest category in the comparison. Printful's in-house model means one QA standard across its 12 fulfillment centers, industry-leading DTG and embroidery output, and a documented reshipment rate under a quarter of a percent. When an order fails, one company reprints and reships on its own authority.

Gelato doesn't own its printers but manages its 140+ partners to shared standards, with centralized order monitoring. Real-world quality reviews are consistently strong — especially for wall art, where its output is considered gallery-grade — and because production happens locally, items spend less time in transit, which itself reduces damage rates. For most products, customers will not tell the difference; for embroidery and premium apparel, Printful still holds a visible edge.

Shipping Speed & Global Fulfillment

Gelato wins on global shipping: 90% of its orders are produced locally in the destination country via automatic routing, while Printful ships from 12 fixed centers with 2–5 business day production.

Printful's model is predictable: orders route to the nearest of its centers in the US, Mexico, Canada, the UK, and the EU, production runs a consistent 2–5 business days, and US delivery typically completes in 5–10 business days. Within its coverage zones it is fast and reliable; outside them — Asia-Pacific, South America, much of the rest of the world — orders become international shipments with customs and long transit.

Gelato's distributed network flips this. With 140+ hubs in 32 countries and fully automatic routing, a German customer's order prints in Germany, an Australian's in Australia. Roughly 90% of orders are produced in the destination country, many hubs turn orders around in 24–72 hours of production, and domestic delivery legs are short and cheap. For stores with meaningful non-US/non-EU traffic, this is the decisive advantage of the entire comparison.

Branding & Customization

Printful offers the deepest branding toolkit in POD — custom inside/outside labels, pack-ins, branded packaging, and branded tracking; Gelato+ covers branded inserts only.

If the unboxing experience is part of your brand, this category alone can settle the decision. Printful supports woven and printed labels, hang tags, pack-ins like stickers and thank-you cards, custom packaging, and a branded tracking page — the fullest white-label experience available in print-on-demand. Gelato+ includes branded inserts and packaging options on paid plans, which covers the basics at a lower price, but the depth isn't comparable. Premium brand builders choose Printful here.

Integrations & Selling Channels

Both integrate natively with Shopify, Etsy, WooCommerce, Wix, and Squarespace — a tie for mainstream sellers, with minor differences at the edges.

Printful adds native Amazon and eBay support; Gelato adds BigCommerce and is particularly smooth on Etsy. Both offer mature APIs, automatic order sync, and tracking push-back. Both dashboards are beginner-friendly; Gelato's is slightly simpler since there is no facility-selection logic to think about, while Printful's offers more product-personalization tooling (its mockup generator and personalization features are strong for customized-gift stores).

Customer Support

Both platforms resolve issues through a single accountable company — Printful for its own factories, Gelato for its partner network — making this a rare category where both beat marketplace-style competitors.

Both offer 24/7 support and, crucially, both own the resolution when an order arrives misprinted. Printful reprints in-house; Gelato manages the partner that produced the item, but the seller never negotiates with a third party directly. Sellers coming from provider-marketplace platforms consistently cite this single-point accountability as a reason to choose either of these two.

Real Cost Example: A T-Shirt in the US, and a Framed Poster in Germany

On a US-delivered tee, Gelato lands around $11.50 all-in versus Printful's $15–17; on international wall art, Gelato's local production widens the gap to $5–10 per order.

Take the standard benchmark: a classic cotton tee delivered to a US customer. Gelato's 2026 base cost is roughly $6.96 plus ~$4.54 US shipping — about $11.50 delivered. Printful's equivalent typically lands at $15–17. On a $24.99 Etsy tee, that's a $3.50–5.50 margin difference per order before subscription discounts. Printful Growth's up-to-33% discount closes much of it at volume, but not all.

Now run Gelato's home turf: a framed poster sold to a customer in Germany. Gelato prints it in the EU at local cost and ships domestically — no customs, 2–5 day delivery. Printful would fulfill from its EU centers (Latvia/Spain) competently for EU destinations, but destinations beyond its 12-center footprint revert to cross-border shipping. The pattern is consistent: Printful is competitive inside its zones and premium-priced everywhere; Gelato is competitive almost everywhere and premium nowhere.

Real-World Scenarios: Which Should You Choose?

Brand builders selling premium apparel should choose Printful; international sellers and wall-art stores should choose Gelato; many scaling brands use both.

  • Premium apparel brand on Shopify: Choose Printful. Embroidery quality, custom labels, pack-ins, and branded packaging justify the 15–35% base-cost premium when your retail price carries a brand markup.
  • Store with global traffic (EU, UK, APAC): Choose Gelato. Local production in 32 countries converts better, delivers faster, and avoids customs friction — the single biggest international conversion lever in POD.
  • Wall art, posters, stationery, photo products: Choose Gelato. Its paper-and-canvas catalog is the strongest in the industry, printed near your buyers.
  • Embroidery-heavy or cut-and-sew line: Choose Printful — Gelato barely competes here.
  • Hybrid scaling brand: Run hero/branded products on Printful and route international orders plus wall art through Gelato. Both connect to the same store, and orders flow by product.

How We Compared Them

This comparison draws on our hands-on reviews of both platforms (linked below), official pricing pages as of mid-2026, and independent 2026 analyses for base-cost differentials (Printful's 15–35% premium), reshipment rates, and network coverage (Gelato's 32 countries, 90% local production, 24–72 hour hub turnaround). Figures reflect published 2026 rates; we update this page when either platform changes plans or networks.

Final Verdict

Printful and Gelato are both quality-first platforms, and you will not disaster-proof your store by picking either — the real question is where your customers are and what your brand promises. Printful is the brand platform: in-house quality control, the deepest branding toolkit in POD, and flawless execution inside its fulfillment zones, at a premium price. Gelato is the global platform: lower base costs, a curated quality catalog led by wall art, and a local-production network that makes a Berlin order feel like a Berlin business. Both are free to start. Order one sample of your flagship product from each, run the delivered-cost math for your top three destination countries, and the right answer will be obvious.

faqs.q: Is Gelato cheaper than Printful?
faqs.a: Yes, on both subscriptions and base costs. faqs.q: Which has better print quality, Printful or Gelato?

Gelato's vetted partner network is very close behind and is considered gallery-grade for wall art — for most products, customers won't notice a difference. Printful's clearest quality wins are embroidery and premium apparel.

faqs.q: Is Printful or Gelato better for international orders?

faqs.q: Which ships faster, Printful or Gelato?
faqs.a: Gelato is typically faster globally: many hubs turn production around in 24–72 hours and deliver domestically in 2–5 business days. Printful produces in 2–5 business days with US delivery typically completing in 5–10 business days. faqs.q: Can I use both Printful and Gelato at the same time?

faqs.q: Is Printful Growth or Gelato+ worth it first?
